newsitem.title: CHINA: China B share trading seen volatile short-term.
newsitem.headline: China B share trading seen volatile short-term.

text.p: China's foreign currency B shares will gain over the long term but trading could be highly volatile over the next month, a Credit Lyonnais Securities (Asia) Ltd analyst said on Wednesday.
Shanghai and Shenzhen stocks fell heavily on Tuesday and Wednesday due to rumours the government is planning a crackdown on the stock markets, which have risen sharply since January.
"The Chinese bull market still has some more steam -- it still has forward momentum, but it's going to remain highly volatile," said Jing Ulrich, director of China research for the brokerage.

"We advise investors to buy the quality issues, which have strong institutional support, instead of buying stocks which are highly speculative in nature," Ulrich said, declining to name specific companies.
She was speaking to reporters at a China investors' conference organized by Credit Lyonnais in Shanghai.

The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock indices have recently surged on expectations the Chinese authorities would want the markets to be on an upward track before Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on June 30, but talk this week about a crackdown has halted the gains.
In the long run, the outlook for B shares was favourable due to expected strong growth in the Chinese economy, Ulrich said.
"You must be prepared for a roller coaster ride, but the general trend (for the market) is up," she said.
